Can I fit and report this?

Source: vignettes/articles/current-limits.Rmd
current-limits.Rmd

This page answers one question: can I use hsquared for my analysis, and what am I allowed to write in the paper?

hsquared is an experimental package. Most of what follows is not about whether code runs; nearly all of it runs. It is about which numbers have enough evidence behind them to report.

The three-line version

  1. Two default-routed covered paths exist: the univariate Gaussian animal model and t = 2 unstructured multivariate cbind() (validation-scale). Genomic GREML is also covered at validation scale, but only through its explicit engine = "julia", target = "genomic" route; ordinary-call / default-route genomic activation remains held (design-44 G5; BOUNDARY_HOLDOUT_FAIL). Report point estimates only within each stated scope.
  2. Almost everything else fits through an opt-in engine target (some covered at validation scale, some experimental). k≥3 and diagonal multivariate stay experimental. Treat experimental fits as exploratory, or report them beside a comparator you ran yourself.
  3. No standard error or interval in this package is nominally coverage-calibrated. Named univariate pedigree intervals have a narrower directional-conservative claim level, not a nominal-calibration claim. Do not report any interval as if nominal coverage had been established.

Covered at validation scale · experimental · dense · REML-only still means experimental packaging. It is not 1.0 and not interval-calibrated. The ladder caption is dated to this source tree; the live count is validation_status() and this limits page after any covered-row update. This figure does not flip a row. public_covered_count stays 7.

What the status words mean

hsquared uses four words, in descending order of what you may claim. It deliberately never uses a bare “supported”, because that word hides the difference between runs and validated.

Word The code The evidence What you may report
covered Runs Pre-declared recovery gate passed and an external same-estimand comparator agrees Point estimates, within the stated scope
partial Runs Bridge-verified and partly evidenced; the chain has a named hole Exploratory use; report only beside your own comparator
experimental Runs Labelling, not a status tier; every opt-in route carries it Nothing on this package’s word alone
planned Aborts as planned, not implemented None Nothing

This page is the user-facing list of what you may report. validation_status() is a developer evidence table of validation atoms; it is not a complete list of covered routes. Developers can inspect it in their own session:

validation_status()

Do I need Julia?

Yes, for fitting. This matters more here than in most R packages, because the default call is the one that needs it.

What you want What you need
Parse and validate a model, inspect the design matrices and pedigree ordering R only: hs_control(engine = "validate") and model_spec()
Actually fit and get heritability, variance components, EBVs A local Julia, the JuliaCall package, and an HSquared.jl checkout

Without the engine, hsquared() still tells you whether your model is expressible, and errors with install guidance if you ask it to fit. See the engine setup section of the README.

# no Julia required; same ped/dat as the README
hsquared(
  weight ~ sex + animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped),
  data = dat,
  control = hs_control(engine = "validate")
)

model_spec(
  weight ~ sex + animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped),
  data = dat
)

Route-by-route reporting permissions

The cards below are generated from validation_status(), a developer evidence table of validation atoms. They are not a complete list of covered routes — two covered routes have no row there yet and are listed on this page below the cards.

Status Rows What it means for you
covered 6 Pre-declared recovery gate passed and an external same-estimand comparator agrees. Point estimates are reportable within the stated scope.
partial 8 The code runs and is bridge-verified, but the evidence chain is incomplete. Exploratory use only.
planned 7 Not implemented. No reporting permission.

Those counts are rows in the evidence ledger, not user-facing models. Some rows are validation atoms (a pedigree-inverse check, a textbook fixture) or evidence for another row rather than a model you would fit. The cards below are the model routes.

Reader routes

Every route below runs. The question these cards answer is narrower and more useful: what may I put in a paper?

Univariate Gaussian animal model (the default path) 

hsquared(y ~ sex + animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped), data = dat)

Can I fit it? Yes - implemented and covered on the default call.

Can I report the point estimate? Yes, within the stated scope - a pre-declared recovery gate passed and an external same-estimand comparator agrees.

Can I report an interval? Measured, but not nominally calibrated. Named univariate pedigree h2 delta/profile/bootstrap and sigma-a2 profile/bootstrap intervals have a directional-conservative claim level. Sigma-a2 delta/Wald is experimental-only. Do not report any of them as nominal 95% coverage.

Exact scope and caveat. One additive genetic effect, Gaussian response, REML only, fitted by average-information REML on the sparse mixed-model equations. Known-truth recovery is near-unbiased across an h2 grid of 0.2/0.4/0.6; the near-boundary cell h2 = 0.1 shows mild upward bias and 5% boundary pinning. ML is not implemented. REML = FALSE is rejected; use REML = TRUE (the default). That is the same rule for the default fit and for engine = "validate". The covered claim is this REML estimator, not ML. Named h2 delta/profile/bootstrap and sigma-a2 profile/bootstrap intervals are directional-conservative here; sigma-a2 delta/Wald remains experimental-only. None is nominally calibrated.

Concrete fallback. None needed - this is the recommended route. For a model with a second random effect, see the two-effect card below.

Animal model plus independent extra effects (common environment, arbitrary N) 

hsquared(y ~ animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped) + common_env(1 | group),
         data = dat, control = hs_control(engine = "julia"))

Can I fit it? Yes - implemented and covered at validation scale, behind an opt-in engine target.

Can I report the point estimate? Yes, within the stated scope - a pre-declared recovery gate passed and an external same-estimand comparator agrees.

Can I report an interval? No. Standard errors and intervals are asymptotic/delta-method, labelled experimental, and NOT coverage-calibrated. No route in this package currently carries an interval-reporting permission.

Exact scope and caveat. The common-environment leg (additive animal A plus i.i.d. environment, A2 = I) and the arbitrary-N generalization to independent i.i.d. effects are covered at validation scale on a pre-declared 48-seed recovery gate with an external same-estimand REML comparator. The animal-block ratio is narrow-sense h2; other blocks are variance-explained proportions, NOT heritabilities. Independent effects only - correlated, random-regression, and non-Gaussian structures are not this route.

Concrete fallback. The maternal-genetic leg (maternal_genetic(), A2 = pedigree A) runs on the same estimator but is still experimental: its own recovery gate and comparator are owed. Use the covered common-environment route, or treat a maternal fit as exploratory.

Sparse REML variance components (opt-in engine target) 

hsquared(y ~ animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped), data = dat,
         control = hs_control(engine = "julia",
           engine_control = list(target = "sparse_reml")))

Can I fit it? Yes, but opt-in and experimental - the code runs; the evidence is incomplete.

Can I report the point estimate? Not on this package’s evidence alone. Report only beside a comparator you ran yourself, and say the route is experimental.

Can I report an interval? No. Standard errors and intervals are asymptotic/delta-method, labelled experimental, and NOT coverage-calibrated. No route in this package currently carries an interval-reporting permission.

Exact scope and caveat. Reaches the same REML optimum as the default path and is cross-checked against an independent pure-R REML optimizer and the external pedigreemm package. It exists as an engine-target check, not as a separate user-facing model.

Concrete fallback. Use the default hsquared() call, which is the covered route to the same estimates.

Repeatability / permanent environment (repeated records) 

hsquared(y ~ animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped) + permanent(1 | id), data = dat,
         control = hs_control(engine = "julia"))

Can I fit it? Yes, but opt-in and experimental - the code runs; the evidence is incomplete.

Can I report the point estimate? Not on this package’s evidence alone. Report only beside a comparator you ran yourself, and say the route is experimental.

Can I report an interval? No. Standard errors and intervals are asymptotic/delta-method, labelled experimental, and NOT coverage-calibrated. No route in this package currently carries an interval-reporting permission.

Exact scope and caveat. REML-only repeatability optimizer returning additive, permanent-environment, and residual variances. Va and Vpe are only identifiable with repeated records per individual. No comparator and no known-truth recovery gate yet.

Concrete fallback. Fit the covered univariate animal model on individual means, or run your own comparator (for example sommer) alongside before reporting.

Genomic (GREML) and single-step relationship models 

hsquared(y ~ genomic(1 | id, markers = M), data = dat,
         control = hs_control(engine = "julia",
           engine_control = list(target = "genomic")))

Can I fit it? Yes - implemented and covered at validation scale, behind an opt-in engine target.

Can I report the point estimate? Yes, within the stated scope - a pre-declared recovery gate passed and an external same-estimand comparator agrees.

Can I report an interval? No. Standard errors and intervals are asymptotic/delta-method, labelled experimental, and NOT coverage-calibrated. No route in this package currently carries an interval-reporting permission.

Exact scope and caveat. 0.7 covered claim is opt-in genomic GREML only (target = “genomic”; genomic_variance_ratio on K_lambda; design-51/53). Accepts supplied Ginv or builds VanRaden1 G from markers. Ordinary-call / default-route activation remains held (design-44 G5; BOUNDARY_HOLDOUT_FAIL). Single-step / metafounder paths in this combined validation_status row remain exploratory (not the 0.7 covered claim). APY / production / intervals out of scope.

Concrete fallback. Report genomic_variance_ratio on the declared kernel with the no-anchor and scale disclosures. Do not treat single-step or default genomic routing as covered.

SNP-BLUP marker effects 

hsquared(y ~ genomic(1 | id, markers = M), data = dat,
         control = hs_control(engine = "julia",
           engine_control = list(target = "snp_blup")))

Can I fit it? Yes, but opt-in and experimental - the code runs; the evidence is incomplete.

Can I report the point estimate? Not on this package’s evidence alone. Report only beside a comparator you ran yourself, and say the route is experimental.

Can I report an interval? No. Standard errors and intervals are asymptotic/delta-method, labelled experimental, and NOT coverage-calibrated. No route in this package currently carries an interval-reporting permission.

Exact scope and caveat. VanRaden method-1 marker model returning per-marker effects, genomic breeding values, and fixed effects, with variances either supplied or REML-estimated. Weighted/Bayesian marker priors and JWAS/sommer/BLUPF90 parity are planned.

Concrete fallback. Use the genomic GREML route above for a breeding-value question, and treat marker effects as exploratory.

Multivariate Gaussian animal model (cbind response) 

hsquared(cbind(y1, y2) ~ animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped), data = dat)
# routes on the default path; engine = "julia", target = "multivariate" still works

Can I fit it? Yes - implemented and covered on the default call.

Can I report the point estimate? Yes, within the stated scope - a pre-declared recovery gate passed and an external same-estimand comparator agrees.

Can I report an interval? No. Standard errors and intervals are asymptotic/delta-method, labelled experimental, and NOT coverage-calibrated. No route in this package currently carries an interval-reporting permission.

Exact scope and caveat. REML-only, animal-model-only, dense/validation-scale. Returns G0/R0 covariance and correlation matrices, per-trait h2, and cross-trait EBVs. Covered claim is t = 2 unstructured G0/R0 only (2026-09-02 maintainer sign-off); k>=3 and genetic_structure = “diagonal” stay experimental. The R-lane evidence includes a 100-replicate t = 2 cold-start recovery study, one reproduced full-unstructured sommer comparator leg, a published Mrode-style supplied-variance anchor, and a Bayesian MCMCglmm agreement probe - which is NOT same-estimand REML parity. The Mrode anchor is SUPPLIED-covariance (fixed effects and BLUPs given known G0/R0), so it does NOT anchor the ESTIMATED G0/R0, and no published textbook anchor for estimated multivariate G0/R0 exists - that evidence is comparator- and recovery-based, not textbook-anchored. R<->engine element-wise parity is verified LOCALLY at pre-declared tolerances, NOT in CI (the CI runner has no Julia, so those checks skip). The engine row is covered; this R-public surface is now covered at validation scale; public_covered_count is 7. Since default routing the cbind route is selected on the default call.

Concrete fallback. For k>=3 or a diagonal genetic structure, treat the fit as experimental. For a single-trait question, use the covered univariate model.

Planned validation lanes and grammar

These rows are planned validation tasks in validation_status(), not a blanket statement that every related fit aborts. Check the partial routes on this page for bounded FA and genetic GLLVM fits. A planned row by itself gives no reporting permission.

  • Mrode fitted animal-model outputs (Phase 1)
  • ASReml comparison policy (Phase 1)
  • BLUPF90/DMU/WOMBAT comparison policy (Phase 1)
  • XSim simulation truth (Phase 5+)
  • genomic and QTL/eQTL validation (Phase 5+)
  • GLLVM-style multivariate validation (Phase 6)
  • CPU/GPU backend comparison (Phase 7+)

Before you report

  1. Confirm this page still lists your route as reportable. Do not treat validation_status() as the complete user list.
  2. Report point estimates for covered routes only.
  3. Do not report a standard error or interval as nominally calibrated. The named univariate-pedigree directional-conservative methods are a narrower claim, not a nominal-coverage permission.
  4. For a partial route, run an external comparator yourself and report both numbers.
  5. Say in the methods that the fit came from an experimental package, and name the version.

Two covered routes without their own status row

validation_status() does not yet carry a separate row for two routes that docs/design/capability-status.md records as covered at validation scale:

  • Random regression / reaction norm, k = 2: animal(rr(age, order = 2) | id, pedigree = ped) via engine_control = list(target = "random_regression"). A pre-declared 48-seed recovery gate passed and a sommer leg() same-estimand comparator agrees on all K_g entries and the residual. k = 2 only. The residual is homogeneous and there is no permanent-environment term, so rr_heritability() can overstate h²(t) for repeated-records designs. K_g values are not comparable across basis-normalization conventions.
  • Direct–maternal correlated 2×2 G: animal(1 | id, pedigree = ped) + maternal_genetic(1 | dam) via engine_control = list(target = "direct_maternal"). A pre-declared 48-seed gate passed and a sommer covm() same-estimand comparator agrees. heritability() returns the labelled Willham triple: direct h²_d, maternal m², total h²_T, and r_am; never a bare scalar. Direct h² is not the total heritability, and a negative r_am is real and expected. Single relationship A only.

Both are opt-in, experimental, REML-only, and dense (n ≲ 1000); unlike the default animal() route and target = "repeatability", neither currently accepts engine_control$max_dense_cells, so this n is a recommendation here, not an engine-enforced cap. Read this page before reporting a number; validation_status() is a developer evidence table. The cards above are generated from the evidence table and will not mention them until those rows exist.

New partial FA and genetic GLLVM routes

The four-trait, one-factor Gaussian pedigree FA fit is available through an explicit Julia expert-control target. It returns a fitted genetic covariance, uniqueness estimates, genetic correlations, and diagnostics. The rank does not by itself identify every loading and uniqueness configuration. The tested fixture required a higher iteration limit. In a 200-seed Gaussian pedigree study with four traits and three records per animal, 141 fits converged and 110 met the declared covariance-recovery diagnostics, using two ordinary starts with 5000 iterations each. All 200 attempts were counted. Inspect convergence, start disagreement and floor diagnostics before interpreting a fit. See Multivariate Gaussian animal models for the exact call and the study’s limits.

The three-trait, two-factor Poisson-log pedigree genetic GLLVM fit is also an explicit expert-control route. It returns genetic covariance and correlations plus trait-level conditional genetic modes on the log-rate scale. See Genetic GLLVM opt-in for the exact call and limits.

Both routes are partial. Use their point estimates for exploration; for a paper, run a suitable comparator yourself. No interval, automatic factor rank, missing-response fit, or broader family claim follows from these cells.
